set.next_deadline: No open PBV RFP as of November 8, 2026. HACN selects PBV owner proposals by advertised RFP under 24 CFR 983.51(b)(1) or without competition under 983.51(b)(2) for projects selected through a competitive public funding process within the prior three years; developers request PBVs after a CTCAC, HCD or HOME award.
set.cycle_notes: Rolling, request-driven. The comprehensive Administrative Plan rewrite (HOTMA and NSPIRE) presented to the HACN board February 3, 2026 and targeted for April 7, 2026 was not adopted then; the April 7, 2026 agenda carried only the FY 2026-27 Annual Plan, and the October 6, 2026 board report says comprehensive updates are still underway. The 2021 Administrative Plan remains in effect, amended October 6, 2026 for Chapter 16 payment standards (EHV standards cut from 120% to the 90-110% FMR range per Notice PIH 2026-20; 2027 payment standards effective January 1, 2027). Most recent PBV awards in Legistar: Napa Cove (January 2022) and Valley Lodge (February 2022). Next HACN board meeting November 17, 2026.
set.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal Davis-Bacon wages apply to PBV development activity (new construction or rehab under an Agreement to enter into a HAP contract) involving nine or more contract units, per 24 CFR 983.153(c)(2) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153); PBVs on existing housing with no development activity do not trigger it, and state prevailing wage is not triggered by PBVs alone. The HACN 2021 Administrative Plan requires PBV advertisements to state labor standards compliance.

reason: Planned April 7, 2026 Administrative Plan rewrite was not adopted (only a Chapter 16 amendment passed October 6, 2026), no PBV RFP is open, and Davis-Bacon applies by 24 CFR 983.153(c)(2) for development of 9 or more contract units.

set.typical_award_size: Adopted October 6, 2026 as Resolution No. 2026-73 (5-0): the City pays water and sewer connection and capacity charges (about $28,500 per ADU) from Measure D for the first six ADUs or JADUs with complete building permit applications each calendar year, first come first served, one per parcel, no tiered incentive; Council omitted the proposed payment of development impact fees for ADUs over 750 square feet. Funded by Measure D subject to annual appropriation. Existing policy and Gov. Code 66311.5 already exempt ADUs of 750 square feet or less from impact fees.
set.per_unit_cap: About $28,500 per ADU (connection and capacity charges only).
set.affordability_requirement: 15-year recorded deed restriction requiring the ADU to be rented at rents affordable to households at or below 160% AMI (per the draft resolution; the adopting motion did not change the AMI level), no rentals under 30 days; violations trigger repayment with interest at the legal judgment rate (10% simple) and a lien.
set.next_deadline: Rolling: first six complete ADU building permit applications each calendar year, first come first served; unused slots do not carry over. No fixed deadline as of November 8, 2026.
set.cycle_notes: Program adopted October 6, 2026 (draft minutes in the October 27, 2026 Council packet, Resolution No. 2026-73). Motion: Measure D subsidies for connection fees only, 6 units a year, 15-year deed restrictions, omit monetary (impact) fees, one per parcel, no tiered incentive. The staff report had proposed 3 units and a 10-year restriction; the draft resolution text said 5 units and 15 years. Final signed resolution text not opened. Chapter 17.37 ADU ordinance amendments were under HCD review as of October 2026. Council reviews the program annually in the budget.
set.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects built on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment or successor agency, or local public housing authority (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720); a homeowner ADU assisted by a City fee payment does not meet those exceptions, although fee payments count as public funds under 1720(b)(4). Confirm with counsel if HACN becomes a party to the agreement.

reason: Council adopted the program October 6, 2026 in changed form (six ADUs a year, connection fees only, 15-year restriction), and Labor Code 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential ADUs on private property.
